blocks.text: Direction — one space-priority model, layered where each concern belongs

content.value: The finished experience: the ACTIVE CONTENT PANE (paper view, document editor) is the protected winner of every layout negotiation — it never drops below a readable measure (~66ch, clamp 55-70ch). All squeeze flows outward by explicit priority: list pane compresses first, then rails to a 44px strip, then the inspector overlays instead of docking; at phone widths the desk becomes a single-pane drill with a breadcrumb trail (nav_path already models drill depth). Resize the window and the desk visibly REASONS about space instead of crushing the middle.

items.value: CSS owns everything CONTINUOUS: container queries on .pane-layout, fluid pane widths via clamp(), fluid typography, inspector auto-overlay, protected content measure. All inline in root.html.heex (Golden Rule 4 respected — style, not script).

The server owns everything DISCRETE/STRUCTURAL: PaneBuilder graduates from index-arithmetic collapse?/3 to an explicit pane ANATOMY model — every pane declares a role (nav | list | content | inspector) and priority; which panes exist, which are rails, and phone drill mode flow from that one model. A tiny width-bucket JS hook (wide | standard | narrow | phone) is the reconciliation seam so server and CSS agree; only bucket TRANSITIONS cross the wire, never raw resize events.

Front B rides the same model: the desk chrome is brought up to the v4/unified-aesthetic bar (tokens, type scale, pane headers, rails, breadcrumb/back affordance for drill navigation), and any survey-proven structure-logic modernization (drill UX, divider/section logic, count badges) lands with it — while Structure.build's gated-tree contracts stay untouched underneath.

Big roster by design: the model decomposes into 10+ independent builder slices (CSS foundation + tokens pass, protected measure, container-query rails, width-bucket hook, PaneBuilder anatomy model, phone drill mode, inspector overlay behavior, breadcrumb navigation, desk restyle, editor/ONIX panel responsiveness, protective tests + view-edit parity guard, studio card update).

content.value: Candidate A — CSS-only responsive layer: container queries + clamp + min-width protections, zero server changes. Cheapest and collision-safest, but it dies on ground truth: collapsed panes are server-rendered different DOM, phone drill requires structural change, and Front B ('upgrade desk structure LOGIC') is explicitly not a styling ask. A CSS-only wave polishes the crush without making the desk smarter — half the wish.

Candidate B — server-first viewport-aware desk: a resize hook streams width to LiveView, PaneBuilder decides everything per width. One authority, maximally smart — but every resize becomes server round-trips (jank under latency, resize storms), continuous sizing genuinely belongs to the browser, and it couples desk logic to transport health. Also the biggest, riskiest diff in the most contract-laden module.

WINNER — the hybrid split-by-layer (space-priority model): discrete structure server-side driven by a BUCKETED width hook (3-4 states, transitions only), continuous adaptation CSS-side, one shared anatomy/priority vocabulary. It wins because it matches where each concern is cheap: browsers are excellent at continuous layout, LiveView is excellent at discrete structure; and it serves BOTH fronts with one model instead of two disconnected workstreams.

Sharpest attack on the winner: TWO COLLAPSE AUTHORITIES. Today's count-based collapse?/3 plus a new width-based display tier can disagree — a pane server-collapsed AND css-railed, or an expand-pane click that auto-re-collapses, oscillating states at bucket boundaries. Absorption: this wave REFACTORS collapse?/3 INTO the anatomy model rather than adding a second mechanism — one state model where the server decides the pane set + roles/priorities and display state derives from (priority x width bucket); the hook exists precisely so both layers read the same discrete mode; hysteresis at bucket edges; and a dedicated survey question maps every current state transition (expand-pane, editor open/close, focus mode) before Decide freezes the state machine.

content.value: The finished experience: the ACTIVE CONTENT PANE (paper view, document editor) is the protected winner of every layout negotiation — it never drops below a readable measure (~66ch, clamp 55-70ch). All squeeze flows outward by explicit priority: list pane compresses first, then rails to a 44px strip, then the inspector overlays instead of docking; at phone widths the desk becomes a single-pane drill with a breadcrumb trail (nav_path already models drill depth). Resize the window and the desk visibly REASONS about space instead of crushing the middle.

items.value: CSS owns everything CONTINUOUS: container queries on .pane-layout, fluid pane widths via clamp(), fluid typography, inspector auto-overlay, protected content measure. All inline in root.html.heex (Golden Rule 4 respected — style, not script).

The server owns everything DISCRETE/STRUCTURAL: PaneBuilder graduates from index-arithmetic collapse?/3 to an explicit pane ANATOMY model — every pane declares a role (nav | list | content | inspector) and priority; which panes exist, which are rails, and phone drill mode flow from that one model. A tiny width-bucket JS hook (wide | standard | narrow | phone) is the reconciliation seam so server and CSS agree; only bucket TRANSITIONS cross the wire, never raw resize events.

Front B rides the same model: the desk chrome is brought up to the v4/unified-aesthetic bar (tokens, type scale, pane headers, rails, breadcrumb/back affordance for drill navigation), and any survey-proven structure-logic modernization (drill UX, divider/section logic, count badges) lands with it — while Structure.build's gated-tree contracts stay untouched underneath.

Big roster by design: the model decomposes into 10+ independent builder slices (CSS foundation + tokens pass, protected measure, container-query rails, width-bucket hook, PaneBuilder anatomy model, phone drill mode, inspector overlay behavior, breadcrumb navigation, desk restyle, editor/ONIX panel responsiveness, protective tests + view-edit parity guard, studio card update).

content.value: Candidate A — CSS-only responsive layer: container queries + clamp + min-width protections, zero server changes. Cheapest and collision-safest, but it dies on ground truth: collapsed panes are server-rendered different DOM, phone drill requires structural change, and Front B ('upgrade desk structure LOGIC') is explicitly not a styling ask. A CSS-only wave polishes the crush without making the desk smarter — half the wish.

Candidate B — server-first viewport-aware desk: a resize hook streams width to LiveView, PaneBuilder decides everything per width. One authority, maximally smart — but every resize becomes server round-trips (jank under latency, resize storms), continuous sizing genuinely belongs to the browser, and it couples desk logic to transport health. Also the biggest, riskiest diff in the most contract-laden module.

WINNER — the hybrid split-by-layer (space-priority model): discrete structure server-side driven by a BUCKETED width hook (3-4 states, transitions only), continuous adaptation CSS-side, one shared anatomy/priority vocabulary. It wins because it matches where each concern is cheap: browsers are excellent at continuous layout, LiveView is excellent at discrete structure; and it serves BOTH fronts with one model instead of two disconnected workstreams.

Sharpest attack on the winner: TWO COLLAPSE AUTHORITIES. Today's count-based collapse?/3 plus a new width-based display tier can disagree — a pane server-collapsed AND css-railed, or an expand-pane click that auto-re-collapses, oscillating states at bucket boundaries. Absorption: this wave REFACTORS collapse?/3 INTO the anatomy model rather than adding a second mechanism — one state model where the server decides the pane set + roles/priorities and display state derives from (priority x width bucket); the hook exists precisely so both layers read the same discrete mode; hysteresis at bucket edges; and a dedicated survey question maps every current state transition (expand-pane, editor open/close, focus mode) before Decide freezes the state machine.

Studio upgrade epic · founding wave · opened 2026-07-19 · epic task filed at Decide

Wave 1 — the space-priority desk

WAVE STATUS: BUILDING. Verification complete (7 deep reports, proofs quoted below). Decisions D1-D18 ratified in the epic charter (.claude/workflows/bp-cloud-epic-charter.md, committed). Epic task studio-space-priority-desk published with 7 wave slices + 6 backlog children. Round 1 (spd-s1, spd-s2, spd-s3) builds now; rounds 2-4 dispatch on merge.

The wish

"We need a lot more smarter responsive logic in studio — [screenshot: paper reader pane crushed to ~15 chars/line between the Papers list pane and the Document inspector]. AND: Please upgrade desk structure logic - it need a great upgrade - it is not up to level with rest of UI anymore." Two fronts, one epic, verified against code before building. FRONT A responsive intelligence: .pane-column is width:260px/min-width:200px/flex-shrink:0 (root.html.heex ~line 1099); the ONLY responsive rules in ~6500 lines of studio CSS are two .bp-paper-surface padding tweaks and two canvas grid collapses; nothing auto-collapses the list pane or inspector when the content pane starves; the reader needs a protected ~55-70ch measure. FRONT B desk structure logic: the tiered desk (Barkpark.Structure.build + PaneBuilder) is judged not up to level with the rest of the UI (the cloud console just got the full GUI-remake treatment). Constraints: inline styles in root.html.heex (Golden Rule 4), .ex/.heex waits for the Elixir Test gate, two concurrent epic cycles (cloud/ GUI-remake finisher; PDS on internal/cli + tenancy) — keep edits to the Studio surface. The user wants a BIG roster: 10+ builder tasks if the verified survey supports it.

Ground truth (read, not guessed)

• The wish's CSS claims CHECK OUT: .pane-layout{display:flex} + .pane-column{width:260px;min-width:200px;flex-shrink:0} at root.html.heex 1098-1100; collapsed strip .pane-column--collapsed{width:44px} at 1272; Document inspector .bp-doc-sidebar.is-open{flex:0 0 300px} at 1469; the only @media rules touching studio are paper-surface padding (3020-3021), canvas grid (3845), reduced-motion, and dark-scheme blocks.
• A server-side collapse mechanism ALREADY EXISTS and is viewport-blind: PaneBuilder.collapse?/3 (pane_builder.ex ~714) implements Sanity-style breadcrumb collapse by pane COUNT (keep last 1-2 full), rendered via <.pane_column collapsed={...}> in studio_live/components.ex ~573 with an expand-pane click event. Count-based, never width-based — the server has zero knowledge of viewport.
• Collapsed panes are DIFFERENT server-rendered DOM (rotated label strip, click target), so a pure-CSS collapse cannot simply reuse them — display state and structure state are entangled today.
• The desk contracts to preserve: Structure.build gated tree drives BOTH Studio panes[0] AND the Go TUI (GET /v1/structure/:dataset); owned_schema_types single harvested map; nav model @canonical capability:studio-nav-model; reveal-via-ancestors + #1851 never-unreachable fallback to the ungated tree.
• The bar for 'up to level': the cloud console v4 language (tokens.json, 5-identity themes, evergreen-mint, Plex Mono machine strings, styleguide canonical + CI drift gate) per the closed GUI-remake design phase; unified-aesthetic epic = ONE token manifest with per-surface emit.
• Prior art in the ledger: studio-structure-polish (COMPLETE — tiered desk, scoped settings), studio-nav-consistency wave 1, task-2532b0a2748e93ba desk-structure review fixes. No epic task exists yet for THIS upgrade — Decide files it.

Direction — one space-priority model, layered where each concern belongs

The finished experience: the ACTIVE CONTENT PANE (paper view, document editor) is the protected winner of every layout negotiation — it never drops below a readable measure (~66ch, clamp 55-70ch). All squeeze flows outward by explicit priority: list pane compresses first, then rails to a 44px strip, then the inspector overlays instead of docking; at phone widths the desk becomes a single-pane drill with a breadcrumb trail (nav_path already models drill depth). Resize the window and the desk visibly REASONS about space instead of crushing the middle.

• CSS owns everything CONTINUOUS: container queries on .pane-layout, fluid pane widths via clamp(), fluid typography, inspector auto-overlay, protected content measure. All inline in root.html.heex (Golden Rule 4 respected — style, not script).
• The server owns everything DISCRETE/STRUCTURAL: PaneBuilder graduates from index-arithmetic collapse?/3 to an explicit pane ANATOMY model — every pane declares a role (nav | list | content | inspector) and priority; which panes exist, which are rails, and phone drill mode flow from that one model. A tiny width-bucket JS hook (wide | standard | narrow | phone) is the reconciliation seam so server and CSS agree; only bucket TRANSITIONS cross the wire, never raw resize events.
• Front B rides the same model: the desk chrome is brought up to the v4/unified-aesthetic bar (tokens, type scale, pane headers, rails, breadcrumb/back affordance for drill navigation), and any survey-proven structure-logic modernization (drill UX, divider/section logic, count badges) lands with it — while Structure.build's gated-tree contracts stay untouched underneath.
• Big roster by design: the model decomposes into 10+ independent builder slices (CSS foundation + tokens pass, protected measure, container-query rails, width-bucket hook, PaneBuilder anatomy model, phone drill mode, inspector overlay behavior, breadcrumb navigation, desk restyle, editor/ONIX panel responsiveness, protective tests + view-edit parity guard, studio card update).

Direction debate

Candidate A — CSS-only responsive layer: container queries + clamp + min-width protections, zero server changes. Cheapest and collision-safest, but it dies on ground truth: collapsed panes are server-rendered different DOM, phone drill requires structural change, and Front B ('upgrade desk structure LOGIC') is explicitly not a styling ask. A CSS-only wave polishes the crush without making the desk smarter — half the wish.

Candidate B — server-first viewport-aware desk: a resize hook streams width to LiveView, PaneBuilder decides everything per width. One authority, maximally smart — but every resize becomes server round-trips (jank under latency, resize storms), continuous sizing genuinely belongs to the browser, and it couples desk logic to transport health. Also the biggest, riskiest diff in the most contract-laden module.

WINNER — the hybrid split-by-layer (space-priority model): discrete structure server-side driven by a BUCKETED width hook (3-4 states, transitions only), continuous adaptation CSS-side, one shared anatomy/priority vocabulary. It wins because it matches where each concern is cheap: browsers are excellent at continuous layout, LiveView is excellent at discrete structure; and it serves BOTH fronts with one model instead of two disconnected workstreams.

Sharpest attack on the winner: TWO COLLAPSE AUTHORITIES. Today's count-based collapse?/3 plus a new width-based display tier can disagree — a pane server-collapsed AND css-railed, or an expand-pane click that auto-re-collapses, oscillating states at bucket boundaries. Absorption: this wave REFACTORS collapse?/3 INTO the anatomy model rather than adding a second mechanism — one state model where the server decides the pane set + roles/priorities and display state derives from (priority x width bucket); the hook exists precisely so both layers read the same discrete mode; hysteresis at bucket edges; and a dedicated survey question maps every current state transition (expand-pane, editor open/close, focus mode) before Decide freezes the state machine.

Survey plan — 16 assignments

• pane-anatomy-css — full CSS anatomy of the desk (pane-layout, pane-column variants, bp-doc-sidebar, editor panels) with every width/flex rule that produces the crush. Why: the CSS foundation slice edits exactly this inventory.
• collapse-state-machine — map collapse?/3 call sites, expand-pane handling, collapsed-pane DOM, every state transition. Why: the refactor into the anatomy model must cover every transition or the two-authorities attack lands.
• width-awareness-seams — existing JS hooks (EditorFocus etc.), app.js structure, LiveView resize/viewport patterns already in the repo. Why: decides how the width-bucket hook ships.
• structure-build-contracts — Structure.build invariants + TUI consumption of GET /v1/structure/:dataset. Why: defines what Front B must NOT touch.
• paper-view-embed — how studio_paper_view sits in the pane flow; which .bp-paper-* classes are shared with the Bulldocs reader/edit surfaces. Why: the protected measure must not drift view-edit parity.
• inspector-sidebar — bp-doc-sidebar open/collapse ownership + persistence. Why: inspector auto-overlay is a flagship slice.
• editor-panels — classic editor + ONIX 60/40 split behavior under squeeze. Why: scoping the editor-responsiveness slice.
• token-bar — does Studio consume design/tokens.json today; gap between root.html.heex CSS vars and the unified-aesthetic manifest; drift-gate implications. Why: defines the concrete 'up to level' restyle.
• nav-model — studio_tabs/StudioChrome topbar behavior at narrow widths; what breadcrumb/drill needs from the nav contract. Why: phone drill mode needs the topbar to cooperate.
• prior-art-bp — ledger deep dive (studio-structure-polish, nav-consistency wave-2 backlog, desk review fixes). Why: don't re-decide the decided or rebuild the rejected.
• concurrent-collision — file footprints of the two running cycles + open PRs touching root.html.heex/studio. Why: the wish's collision constraint needs a verified map, not a hope.
• mobile-drill — actual phone-width behavior today; what single-pane drill needs from handle_params/nav_path. Why: sizes the drill-mode slice honestly.
• resizable-persistence — any persisted-UI-preference machinery precedent (localStorage hooks, user prefs). Why: decides whether pane-width memory is in-scope or deferred.
• test-surface — existing PaneBuilder/StudioLive test coverage + what LiveView tests CAN assert about display state. Why: protective tests per the distrust-vacuous-green doctrine.
• css-organization — structure of the 6500-line inline style block; the canvas-grid collapse precedent; container-query support posture. Why: where the new responsive layer physically lands.
• screenshot-repro — reproduce the crushed-reader scenario live (pane combo + measured widths at common viewports). Why: the wave's acceptance scenario must be reproducible before and after.

Spine

• Epic task: none exists yet — Decide files it and stamps wave_status + wave_paper=studio-responsive-desk-wave-2026-07-19.
• Builder slice tasks: filed at Decide (target 10+ per the wish); each carries wave_paper=studio-responsive-desk-wave-2026-07-19.
• Key code: api/lib/barkpark_web/layouts/root.html.heex (desk CSS) · api/lib/barkpark_web/studio/pane_builder.ex (collapse?/3, build) · api/lib/barkpark/structure.ex (gated tree) · api/lib/barkpark_web/live/studio/studio_live/components.ex (pane render loop, studio_paper_view) · api/lib/barkpark_web/components/studio_components/panes.ex (pane_column).
• Doctrine in force: Golden Rule 4 (inline styles, no blocking head scripts) · Elixir Test gate before merge · main checkout stays on main (builders use worktrees) · view-edit-parity audit after touching .bp-paper-surface.

Survey digest — what 13 reports established (Digest, 2026-07-19)

The survey confirmed the direction's premises with zero fatal contradictions and hardened every fence. The crush is proven twice — statically from the CSS and LIVE on guerrilla with pixel measurements and screenshots: fixed non-shrinking chrome in the default open-paper state totals 604px (44px collapsed root strip + 260px list pane + 300px inspector), the content pane is the ONLY floor-less flex child (.editor-panel flex:1 + .editor-panel-main min-width:0), and .bp-paper-surface's 720px is a ceiling with no floor. Break-even viewport is ~1280px (~66ch); at 900px the reader is ~21ch with heavy hyphenation — the user's screenshot exactly. This is the DEFAULT state of opening any paper, not an edge case.

• RESPONSIVE VACUUM CONFIRMED AND SHARPENED: zero @container/container-type in the whole 6499-line file; 8-9 @media rules, ALL viewport-relative (structurally blind to sibling-pane squeeze); one single <style> block (lines 34-5043), no CSS build pipeline — container queries and clamp() work the instant they are typed. The paper/canvas/sheets region 2967-5009 is a studio-literal-check skip region with its own token families.
• TWO COLLAPSE AUTHORITIES, fully mapped: (A) PaneBuilder.collapse?/3 (pane_builder.ex:725-728) — pure index arithmetic, ONE call site (components.ex:573), stateless, recomputed per render; expand-pane is a NAVIGATION event (nav_path truncation via Scope.expand_pane, scope.ex:161-172), not a toggle. Nine state transitions mapped, incl. keep_full_nav_count flipping 2->1 the instant editor_doc is set. (B) Beta focus mode CSS (html[data-editor-focus=beta] hides .bp-doc-list panes, root.html.heex:1314) driven by editor_mode with NO rebuild_panes interaction — an orthogonal second authority the anatomy model must subsume or explicitly fence.
• WIDTH-BUCKET HOOK IS GREENFIELD WITH A CLEAN LANDING: zero viewport signal reaches LiveView today (all ~17 pushEvent sites checked); single anchor = pane_layout/1's div (panes.ex:33, only .pane-layout in the repo, no hook attached); EditorFocus (root.html.heex:5324) is the mirror-hook template; SgFit the debounce precedent; new code must live inside the existing CSP-nonced inline script block.

Wave 1 — the space-priority desk

WAVE STATUS: BUILDING. Verification complete (7 deep reports, proofs quoted below). Decisions D1-D18 ratified in the epic charter (.claude/workflows/bp-cloud-epic-charter.md, committed). Epic task studio-space-priority-desk published with 7 wave slices + 6 backlog children. Round 1 (spd-s1, spd-s2, spd-s3) builds now; rounds 2-4 dispatch on merge.

The wish

"We need a lot more smarter responsive logic in studio — [screenshot: paper reader pane crushed to ~15 chars/line between the Papers list pane and the Document inspector]. AND: Please upgrade desk structure logic - it need a great upgrade - it is not up to level with rest of UI anymore." Two fronts, one epic, verified against code before building. FRONT A responsive intelligence: .pane-column is width:260px/min-width:200px/flex-shrink:0 (root.html.heex ~line 1099); the ONLY responsive rules in ~6500 lines of studio CSS are two .bp-paper-surface padding tweaks and two canvas grid collapses; nothing auto-collapses the list pane or inspector when the content pane starves; the reader needs a protected ~55-70ch measure. FRONT B desk structure logic: the tiered desk (Barkpark.Structure.build + PaneBuilder) is judged not up to level with the rest of the UI (the cloud console just got the full GUI-remake treatment). Constraints: inline styles in root.html.heex (Golden Rule 4), .ex/.heex waits for the Elixir Test gate, two concurrent epic cycles (cloud/ GUI-remake finisher; PDS on internal/cli + tenancy) — keep edits to the Studio surface. The user wants a BIG roster: 10+ builder tasks if the verified survey supports it.

Ground truth (read, not guessed)

  • The wish's CSS claims CHECK OUT: .pane-layout{display:flex} + .pane-column{width:260px;min-width:200px;flex-shrink:0} at root.html.heex 1098-1100; collapsed strip .pane-column--collapsed{width:44px} at 1272; Document inspector .bp-doc-sidebar.is-open{flex:0 0 300px} at 1469; the only @media rules touching studio are paper-surface padding (3020-3021), canvas grid (3845), reduced-motion, and dark-scheme blocks.
  • A server-side collapse mechanism ALREADY EXISTS and is viewport-blind: PaneBuilder.collapse?/3 (pane_builder.ex ~714) implements Sanity-style breadcrumb collapse by pane COUNT (keep last 1-2 full), rendered via <.pane_column collapsed={...}> in studio_live/components.ex ~573 with an expand-pane click event. Count-based, never width-based — the server has zero knowledge of viewport.
  • Collapsed panes are DIFFERENT server-rendered DOM (rotated label strip, click target), so a pure-CSS collapse cannot simply reuse them — display state and structure state are entangled today.
  • The desk contracts to preserve: Structure.build gated tree drives BOTH Studio panes[0] AND the Go TUI (GET /v1/structure/:dataset); owned_schema_types single harvested map; nav model @canonical capability:studio-nav-model; reveal-via-ancestors + #1851 never-unreachable fallback to the ungated tree.
  • The bar for 'up to level': the cloud console v4 language (tokens.json, 5-identity themes, evergreen-mint, Plex Mono machine strings, styleguide canonical + CI drift gate) per the closed GUI-remake design phase; unified-aesthetic epic = ONE token manifest with per-surface emit.
  • Prior art in the ledger: studio-structure-polish (COMPLETE — tiered desk, scoped settings), studio-nav-consistency wave 1, task-2532b0a2748e93ba desk-structure review fixes. No epic task exists yet for THIS upgrade — Decide files it.

Direction — one space-priority model, layered where each concern belongs

The finished experience: the ACTIVE CONTENT PANE (paper view, document editor) is the protected winner of every layout negotiation — it never drops below a readable measure (~66ch, clamp 55-70ch). All squeeze flows outward by explicit priority: list pane compresses first, then rails to a 44px strip, then the inspector overlays instead of docking; at phone widths the desk becomes a single-pane drill with a breadcrumb trail (nav_path already models drill depth). Resize the window and the desk visibly REASONS about space instead of crushing the middle.

  • CSS owns everything CONTINUOUS: container queries on .pane-layout, fluid pane widths via clamp(), fluid typography, inspector auto-overlay, protected content measure. All inline in root.html.heex (Golden Rule 4 respected — style, not script).
  • The server owns everything DISCRETE/STRUCTURAL: PaneBuilder graduates from index-arithmetic collapse?/3 to an explicit pane ANATOMY model — every pane declares a role (nav | list | content | inspector) and priority; which panes exist, which are rails, and phone drill mode flow from that one model. A tiny width-bucket JS hook (wide | standard | narrow | phone) is the reconciliation seam so server and CSS agree; only bucket TRANSITIONS cross the wire, never raw resize events.
  • Front B rides the same model: the desk chrome is brought up to the v4/unified-aesthetic bar (tokens, type scale, pane headers, rails, breadcrumb/back affordance for drill navigation), and any survey-proven structure-logic modernization (drill UX, divider/section logic, count badges) lands with it — while Structure.build's gated-tree contracts stay untouched underneath.
  • Big roster by design: the model decomposes into 10+ independent builder slices (CSS foundation + tokens pass, protected measure, container-query rails, width-bucket hook, PaneBuilder anatomy model, phone drill mode, inspector overlay behavior, breadcrumb navigation, desk restyle, editor/ONIX panel responsiveness, protective tests + view-edit parity guard, studio card update).

Direction debate

Candidate A — CSS-only responsive layer: container queries + clamp + min-width protections, zero server changes. Cheapest and collision-safest, but it dies on ground truth: collapsed panes are server-rendered different DOM, phone drill requires structural change, and Front B ('upgrade desk structure LOGIC') is explicitly not a styling ask. A CSS-only wave polishes the crush without making the desk smarter — half the wish.

Candidate B — server-first viewport-aware desk: a resize hook streams width to LiveView, PaneBuilder decides everything per width. One authority, maximally smart — but every resize becomes server round-trips (jank under latency, resize storms), continuous sizing genuinely belongs to the browser, and it couples desk logic to transport health. Also the biggest, riskiest diff in the most contract-laden module.

WINNER — the hybrid split-by-layer (space-priority model): discrete structure server-side driven by a BUCKETED width hook (3-4 states, transitions only), continuous adaptation CSS-side, one shared anatomy/priority vocabulary. It wins because it matches where each concern is cheap: browsers are excellent at continuous layout, LiveView is excellent at discrete structure; and it serves BOTH fronts with one model instead of two disconnected workstreams.

Sharpest attack on the winner: TWO COLLAPSE AUTHORITIES. Today's count-based collapse?/3 plus a new width-based display tier can disagree — a pane server-collapsed AND css-railed, or an expand-pane click that auto-re-collapses, oscillating states at bucket boundaries. Absorption: this wave REFACTORS collapse?/3 INTO the anatomy model rather than adding a second mechanism — one state model where the server decides the pane set + roles/priorities and display state derives from (priority x width bucket); the hook exists precisely so both layers read the same discrete mode; hysteresis at bucket edges; and a dedicated survey question maps every current state transition (expand-pane, editor open/close, focus mode) before Decide freezes the state machine.

  • nav-model — studio_tabs/StudioChrome topbar behavior at narrow widths; what breadcrumb/drill needs from the nav contract. Why: phone drill mode needs the topbar to cooperate.
  • prior-art-bp — ledger deep dive (studio-structure-polish, nav-consistency wave-2 backlog, desk review fixes). Why: don't re-decide the decided or rebuild the rejected.
  • concurrent-collision — file footprints of the two running cycles + open PRs touching root.html.heex/studio. Why: the wish's collision constraint needs a verified map, not a hope.
